combatants._comment: Klbkch the Slayer -- Antinium Senior Guardsman, Relc's patrol partner (issue #69: fields as the ALTERNATE early companion in the WATCH-context fights -- crate_scavengers' FORCE path and shield_spiders' cisterns FIGHT path -- while Relc keeps the tutorial/road/inn fights + the deep_tunnels descent, his own arc; no fight fields both). Voice/canon precedent: the #51 gate NPC (data/skeleton_scene.json's `klbkch` entity, whose talk_pool is precise/courteous/dry, never jokey) -- twin shortswords. Stats banded like relc's own record, a notch different in CHARACTER (the harness decides the final numbers, sim_combat_batch.gd ENCOUNTER_CELLS below): dex 16 (>relc's 12) reads as faster/more evasive -- WICombat._resolve_hit's hit_chance formula subtracts the TARGET's dex/4 from the attacker's roll, so a higher-dex ally is genuinely harder for enemies to land a hit on, not mere flavor. str 12 (<relc's 14) and weapon_die 5 (<relc's 6) together read as slightly less raw damage per landed hit (damage = str/2 + roll(weapon_die)) -- lighter twin shortswords vs. a spear. con 18 (<relc's 20) is a notch less bulky than a Drake spearmaster (max_hp = 20+con). `quick_slash` (damage_mult 0.7, 1 AP -- existing skill shape, NO new effect type) is the dual-shortsword flavor grant alongside the shared `basic_swordwork` baseline (same idiom as wilovan's own kit, this file's own record); WICombatAI's melee profile only ever calls power_strike BY NAME (never quick_slash), so this is known-kit flavor, not an AI-exercised skill -- matches the precedent exactly. NO `combat_scale` override: klbkch's field render_scale (data/sprites.json: 0.4348 on a 92px frame, figure crop 69px) already puts his on-screen figure at 69*0.4348=30.0px -- the SAME ~30px standard the Relc containment fix (combat_scale 0.61 on his bespoke 124px Drake frame) exists to force an OVERSIZED rig down to. Klbkch's rig is already standard-sized (Zevara-class per its own sprites.json comment), so no override is needed -- the riverfarm_hunter/antinium_worker precedent (only canon-tall rigs carry combat_scale).

Riverfarm's own ally, `river_wolf_pack`/`briar_collectors`/`briar_collectors_deep` roster (issue #10/#11 FIX-FIRST: Relc has no fictional basis at Riverfarm -- reached solely via a SOLO Door arrival, Liscor's own Watch guardsman, no come-along beat, no locality; see wi-adding-an-encounter's ally precedent). CANON-GROUNDED, ORIGINAL+flag (docs/design/character-profiles-staging.md): wiki.wanderinginn.com/Riverfarm attests a [Hunter] class among the village's defenders (Califfy, Thel Grasse) -- this combatant realizes that attested profession, not an invented one. Stats/weapon_die/ai/skills are an EXACT clone of `relc`'s block (same numbers, only id/display_name/sprite differ) -- R2/R3's tuned harness bands (sim_combat_batch.gd RIVERFARM_CELLS, gated 0.55-0.95/0.55-0.85, measured 0.84) were tuned against this exact stat block under the old id; changing any stat here invalidates them. No `combat_scale` override (unlike relc's 0.61, which contains his bespoke 124px Drake frame) -- the `a_hunter` sprite is a plain 64px human frame, same convention as every other human-sized combatant. Fields only when `hunter_will_come` is banked (data/dialogue/riverfarm_hunter.json's own come-along beat, at the village) -- never on `met_relc` alone.

Issue #24 (HR-II forward-ref): the Rock Crab, a T1 floodplains renewable cull target (region-tiers.md/sim_combat_batch.gd's own tier table -- floodplains is T1, expected build warrior1-4). Design identity per the wiki-verified staging profile (character-profiles-staging.md Home-Region II): boulder-mimic, ARMORED and SLOW, not a swarm -- damage_reduction 8 is the identity stat and is LOCKED by controller ruling (this file's only other dr holder is vault_construct, a T4 boss, at 3; rock_crab is the first LOW-tier dr carrier), dex low models 'slow' (WICombat's hit_chance formula subtracts the TARGET's dex/4 from the attacker's roll -- low dex means genuinely easier to land a hit on, not flavor). str/weapon_die carry real crushing-pincer damage on the hits that DO land -- canon calls it dangerous enough that 'goblin hunting packs kill them WITH casualties'. No skills (a single armored brawler, not a caster/support). TUNING TRAP 1 (band): the first SOLO-single-enemy GATED cell below T4 -- a plain low-con/low-dr draft (con 7, dr 2) read 1.00 win_rate / 2 median rounds vs warrior2+relc, nowhere near band; dr 8 + real hp is what holds it. TUNING TRAP 2 (relc_downed -- the STRUCTURAL frontier, measured across ~30 candidate stat combos at the real 100-seed gate): for ANY single-melee-enemy roster vs warrior2+relc, win_rate<=0.95 and relc_downed<=0.5 are jointly INFEASIBLE -- PC death is the ONLY defeat (_check_end) and the melee AI always focuses the lowest-HP player-sider, which is ALWAYS relc (hp 40 < pc's 44), so a loss requires the crab to chew through relc FIRST and still kill the pc: every combo weak enough to spare relc most fights reads win 0.96-1.00 (out of band), every in-band combo downs relc >=~0.55. The whole measured frontier: win 0.91<->downed 0.60, 0.93<->0.62, 0.95<->0.59, 0.96<->0.53, 0.98<->0.50. Shipped point (the review-wave FIX-FIRST retune, offense DOWN from the first-landed str 16/die 10/con 20 whose relc_downed=0.83 was the harness's highest): str 14 (down 2), weapon_die 10 (held), con 16 (hp 36, down from 40) -- gate read win_rate=0.93 / median=4 / relc_downed=0.62 (from 0.83). A future pass wanting downed <=0.5 must change STRUCTURE, not stats: per-cell band floor-raise (the alley_footpads 0.75-0.98 low-lethality precedent) or a windup/slam cadence (halves swing count on declare rounds; the harness melee pc never dodges a telegraph, so spike lethality survives) -- both need a controller ruling. combat_scale 3.57 contains the field sprite's oversized render_scale (data/sprites.json rock_crab: render_scale 2.57 targets ~36px FIELD presence off a 14px crop; combat_scale multiplies the SAME crop to ~50px for the close-range arena read, canon's 'shell the size of a cart' -- the same per-combatant override mechanism relc/vault_construct/ruin_guardian use, REPLACING not stacking with render_scale, per board_renderer.gd's own contract).

Canon Liscor-area ambush predator (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Shield_Spiders -- black-and-silver armored carapace, Silver-rank individually, nest under Liscor's Dungeon). A goblin_raider-class melee reskin nudged toward the carapace fantasy: +con (armored back), +dex (ambusher), lower int/cha. SPRITE STAND-IN: uses `bat` (the only dark cave-creature sheet in-tree) -- flagged in docs/VISUAL-LOG.md for a real arachnid sprite (Track B / PixelLab). str/weapon_die tuned down from an earlier reading: the nest's ['shield_spider','shield_spider'] roster now correctly fields TWO distinct combatants (WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id rosters at build time) instead of silently collapsing to one, so `cisterns_fight`'s warrior-L1-SOLO clear is a genuine 2-spider fight -- these numbers keep that findable (real risk, not free) without trivializing the ally-backed/level-2 approaches. Balance is MEASURED-only in sim_combat_batch.gd's ENCOUNTER_CELLS (see report).

The sewers' weak trash pack. Wiki lacks a named sewer-rat monster, so realized SPRITE-HONESTLY as cave bats (`bat` sheet, same as cave_spider's 'Cave Bat') -- canon-plausible tunnel vermin, flagged generic-diegetic per the spec. Deliberately fragile (low con/weapon_die) so the sewers_walkthrough autoplay clears it fast.

Raskghar scout -- canon nocturnal cave predator (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Raskghar): a cross between an upright bear and a lion, towers over Gnolls, tracks and ambushes prey. FICTION FLOOR (binding on any future retune): an elite Raskghar must STRICTLY dominate a plain goblin_raider on every combat axis -- currently str 11>10, con 14>9, weapon_die 5>4. If the boss band ever needs this fight easier, cut the BOSS's own numbers (see raskghar_awakened), never below raider-dominance here. A bruiser-class melee pair, low int/cha. Serves DOUBLE duty -- the deep_tunnels route-fight pair AND the 2 scout adds in the Awakened's boss roster (its ['raskghar_scout','raskghar_scout'] entry now correctly fields TWO distinct combatants -- WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id rosters at build time). Down from the earlier str 15/con 20/die 7 reading: those values were calibrated while the boss roster silently fielded only ONE scout, so each scout carried double weight; with the pair real, awakened_boss_w2_relc's 0.6-0.75 band splits its difficulty budget across three bodies -- the bulk of the cut went to the boss's own HP/die, the remainder here, keeping raider-dominance intact. The route-fight cells (measured-only, no band) read easier than under the old inflated statline, which is fine. combat_scale 0.4492 contains the hulking 124px frame at the feet (the Relc containment lesson); sprite is a real directional PixelLab v2 idle/walk/slice set. Balance MEASURED-only in sim_combat_batch.gd SCOUT_CELLS; GATED via BOSS_CELLS (see raskghar_awakened's own comment).

The Awakened Raskghar BOSS -- canon (a Raskghar that ate a Gnoll's heart, permanently smarter, matches a Level-20 warrior). High-HP bruiser (con 30 -> 50 max_hp). Its signature [Raskghar Maul] is a reaching slowed-rider swing on the EXISTING spell_damage+applies machinery (NO new effect type). `ai: caster` is REQUIRED, not decorative: the melee AI only fires attack/power_strike by name, so a `caster` boss (leads with the range-2 maul, falls through to claws) is the only shipped profile that actually LANDS the slow without a combat_ai.gd change. combat_scale 0.4839 lets it loom ~2 cells while HP bars stay readable. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd BOSS_CELLS -- GATED 0.6-0.75 vs warrior2+Relc, measured solo. The boss ENCOUNTER entity (party/veto beat) is separate from this combatant + arena + harness band. con/weapon_die carry the bulk of the band's difficulty budget by design: the two scout adds have a fiction FLOOR (must dominate a goblin_raider -- see raskghar_scout), so when the band needs the 3-vs-2 fight easier the boss's own HP/die move first. The earlier con 44/die 9 reading was calibrated while the roster silently fielded only ONE scout add; with both real, this record returned to its original design point and the band re-verified at 0.68.

The rift_vermin_leak trash swarm (beat-2, inn-cellar-adjacent; the entity placement lives in skeleton_scene.json). CANON-PLAUSIBLE, wiki.wanderinginn.com/Magical_Rats: 'Magical Rats' are rodents drawn to ambient/leaking magic ('any place with magic'), display diverse powers incl. fire breath -- the anchor-stone's residual rift-link leaking mana into the cellar is exactly the draw the wiki describes, so this is a direct thematic fit realized generic-diegetically (no single named subspecies is attested for a plain magic-drawn rat swarm). Two 'coward' twins (rift_vermin_a/b, letter-suffix convention per training_dummy_a/b) + one ranged 'ember-touched' caster (rift_vermin_c, EXISTING flame_bolt skill -- the canon fire-breath power, no new skill.json entry). SPRITE STAND-IN: reuses `bat` (same convention as cave_spider/sewer_vermin, VISUAL-LOG flagged for a real rodent sheet). Given DISTINCT ids rather than repeating one id 2-3x in an encounter's `enemies` array -- a duplicate-id roster now fields every listed combatant correctly (WICombat._init dedups same-catalog-id entries with a runtime suffix), but hand-authored distinct ids stay the clearer convention for a new multi-enemy roster: no suffix ever shows up in an event/snapshot id stream, and each individual can carry its own kit (rift_vermin_c's flame_bolt) without a shared-template constraint. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd RUIN_CELLS, GATED 0.55-0.95 at the warrior5_mage5 (~L10, 'L8-12 kit') representative build. ISSUE #83 ADOPTION: `ai` changed melee -> `coward` -- a swarm-rat scattering once hurt (flees under 30% hp, regroups toward its nest-mates) is the natural read for 'vermin', and rift_vermin_leak's wide GENERIC 0.55-0.95 band (see sim_combat_batch.gd's own header table) gives real margin to absorb the behavior shift; re-derived in-band, before/after logged on sim_combat_batch.gd's PARTY/RUIN_CELLS comment block.

Rift_vermin_leak's second twin -- see rift_vermin_a's _comment for the full canon cite + distinct-id rationale + the issue #83 `coward` adoption. Identical stat template (a matched pair), given its own id per that convention (not required for a correct fielding anymore, but keeps ids suffix-free and each individual independently reskinnable).

Rift_vermin_leak's ranged member -- the canon 'fire breath' power (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Magical_Rats) realized via the EXISTING `flame_bolt` skill (goblin_shaman's spell_damage/range-4 bolt, no new skill.json entry -- flame is flame regardless of caster). `ai: ranged` so combat_ai.gd's ranged profile actually fires it (see wi-adding-an-encounter's autoplay gotcha: a melee-profile combatant never casts).

Ruin_guardian -- the anchor-stone pedestal's warden (beat-3 recovery run; the entity lives in ruin_surface, the pedestal gate is wired separately). CANON-CITE, wiki.wanderinginn.com/Chapter_3.07_H (+ wiki.wanderinginn.com/Thresk): the Ruins of Albez house a guardian construct/Golem the Horns of Hammerad fought at Warmage Thresk's treasury door -- 'a White-Hot Flame Golem', humanoid, animate flame with a mana-stone core, immensely dangerous at Horns' (much higher) power level. THIS combatant is NOT that same already-narratively-resolved construct (it was destroyed on-page; reusing it verbatim would also be far too strong for a ~L10 recovery-run gate) -- it's CANON-PLAUSIBLE: Albez is described as 'a breeding ground for Monsters' riddled with 'several dungeons' on a leyline, so a lesser ward-construct of the same animate-guardian family, sentineling a DIFFERENT anchor-stone pedestal elsewhere in the ruins, is a direct, non-colliding extrapolation of the same lore (construct/undead-class per the plan brief -- realized construct-side, no new mechanic). `ai: melee` (no new skill needed -- `tough_body`, an EXISTING skill, supplies the construct's durability flavor as flat +10 hp). SPRITE STAND-IN: `training_dummy` (an already-animate humanoid-shaped combat prop reads as a plausible guardian effigy without colliding with any established character's sprite -- reusing raskghar_awakened's or a goblin's sprite here was explicitly avoided per CLAUDE.md's stray-sprite-reuse gotcha). combat_scale looms it slightly above the escort wards. Balance: sim_combat_batch.gd RUIN_CELLS, adjudicated win_lo/win_hi like deep_descent's raskghar_awakened (Relc-escorted cell explicitly banded, solo cell measured-only hard-mode frontier). ISSUE #83 RE-BAND: `con` 28 -> 24 (max_hp -4) -- its own escort wards (ruin_ward_a/b) adopted the new `guard` profile, which clusters them near whichever of their side is hurt worst instead of rushing the party individually; against THIS roster the effect made the fight measurably harder (`ruin_guardian_w8_relc` win_rate 0.69 -> 0.54, dropping the gated 0.55-0.8 floor by 0.01). Shortening the guardian's OWN hp (not the wards') restores `ruin_guardian_w8_relc` to 0.59, back in band with real margin; ruin_guardian_w8_solo (measured) moved 0.01 -> 0.09 alongside it. Re-verified via sim_combat_batch.gd. (The trapped_halls snare no longer shares ruin_ward_a/b at all -- it fields the melee-ai `snare_ward_a/b` clones, see snare_ward_a's own comment -- so this record's stats now serve exactly ONE gated cell.)

Ruin_guardian's first escort ward -- see ruin_guardian's _comment for the full canon cite. A lesser attendant construct (deep_warren boss+2-scouts structure precedent), given its OWN id (not repeated) per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a. ISSUE #83 ADOPTION: `ai` changed melee -> `guard` -- an attendant construct body-blocking for whichever of its own side (the guardian, or its sibling ward) is hurt worst is the direct mechanical reading of 'escort ward'. Fielded ONLY in the ruin_guardian roster (RUIN_CELLS' GATED 0.55-0.8 relc cell, re-derived in-band -- see sim_combat_batch.gd's own comment block): the trapped_halls snare originally reused this id too, but the guard profile has no boss to escort there (the wards clustered around each other/rift_vermin_c instead of engaging, eroding the FIGHT route's cost to 0.94 -- the SAME illusory-cost failure the 8d C1 review's roster-only ruling fixed once already), so the snare now fields `snare_ward_a`/`snare_ward_b` (below): stat clones of this record with plain melee ai. TRAP: one shared combatant id cannot serve two contexts wanting different behavior -- there is no per-encounter AI override, and the two gated cells were edge-pinned in OPPOSITE directions off this one id.

Ruin_guardian's second escort ward -- identical template to ruin_ward_a (a matched pair), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a; carries the SAME issue #83 `guard` adoption, see ruin_ward_a's own comment.

The trapped_halls snare's ward, a stat CLONE of ruin_ward_a with plain `melee` ai instead of ruin_ward_a's issue-#83 `guard` profile. WHY A SEPARATE ID EXISTS (the ONLY difference is the ai field): one shared combatant id cannot serve both the guardian-escort context (which wants `guard` -- body-block the boss) and the snare context (which wants ENGAGEMENT -- no boss to escort there, so guard-profile wards clustered around each other/rift_vermin_c instead of fighting, eroding the FIGHT route's cost from 0.69 to 0.94 win_rate, the exact illusory-cost failure the 8d C1 review's roster-only ruling fixed once already) -- and the two gated cells (RUIN_CELLS' ruin_guardian_w8_relc 0.55-0.8, DUNGEON_CELLS' trapped_halls_snare_t4_solo 0.55-0.95) were edge-pinned in OPPOSITE directions off that one shared id. There is no per-encounter AI override mechanism; a distinct id IS the override, same roster-only pattern. Same 'Lesser Ward' display_name/sprite -- players see the identical construct, the split is internal bookkeeping. Any future ruin_ward_a stat retune must be mirrored here BY HAND (drift trap: no inheritance exists in this catalog).

The trapped_halls snare's second ward -- identical template to snare_ward_a (a matched pair, same as the ruin_ward_a/b pairing it clones), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a. See snare_ward_a's own comment for why these clones exist at all.

Briar collector, `briar_collectors` encounter roster (the hollow's shallow wave). Canon-cite: wiki.wanderinginn.com/Plants -- Birevine ('vines stronger than steel rope, covered in razor-sharp thorns'); this roster is the witch's craft animating that plant into a debt-collecting construct, not an invented species. High con/moderate str (woody, grabs and squeezes), low dex (rooted, doesn't dodge) and minimal int/wis/cha (mindless while animate). No skills -- a plain thorn-lash `attack()`, escalation is `briar_collector_deep`'s job. Own sprite (`briar_collector`, plant-flavored) rather than a cross-species reuse.

Briar_collectors' second member -- see briar_collector_a's _comment for the full canon cite. Identical stat template (a matched pair, same convention as rift_vermin_a/b), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented there.

Deep briar collector, `briar_collectors_deep` encounter roster (the escalated second wave of the same hollow fight, arena `witch_hollow` shared with `briar_collectors` -- same canon-cite as briar_collector_a). Tougher template: higher con/str and `power_strike` (a heavier constricting grab, the EXISTING skill goblin_chieftain already uses -- no new skill.json entry) so the wave reads as a genuine step up rather than a reskinned repeat. Own sprite (`briar_collector_deep`, deliberately darker/taller) carries the escalation visually too. ISSUE #66 (region tiers): con raised (a/b: 24/26 -> 38/40) so `briar_collectors_deep_t3_spellsword9_hunter` (sim_combat_batch.gd RIVERFARM_CELLS, GATED 0.55-0.85 against the T3 reference build) holds its band -- `briar_collectors_w10_hunter`'s old `warrior5_mage5` cell is now the measured pre-tier baseline; see docs/design/region-tiers.md.

Briar_collectors_deep's second member -- see briar_collector_deep_a's _comment for the canon cite + escalation rationale. Plain (no power_strike, slightly higher con instead) so the wave isn't two simultaneous 2x-multiplier hitters -- one heavy striker plus one bulkier grappler, same asymmetric-pair shape as goblin_ambush's raider+shaman. Given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.

River wolf, `river_wolf_pack` roster (arena `village_edge_night`, spawns only under the night phase gate -- unreachable at day by design). Canon-cite: wiki.wanderinginn.com/Monsters -- Wilwolf (an attested wild-wolf monster whose fur is harvested as a crafting material, i.e. ordinary huntable wildlife, not the goblin-tamed Carn Wolf subspecies). Faster/leaner than the briar collectors (higher dex, lower con) -- a pack hunter that closes quickly rather than a rooted grappler. No skills; river_wolf_c (the pack's alpha) carries the roster's only power_strike. ISSUE #83 ADOPTION: `ai` changed melee -> `skirmisher` on the two flanking wolves (river_wolf_a/b) -- a fast pack hunter nipping in for a bite then darting clear before the target can retaliate is the same 'closes quickly' read this comment already establishes, just extended to the retreat half; the alpha (river_wolf_c) stays plain `melee` (holds the line, doesn't disengage), so the pack now mixes two profiles instead of three identical fighters. `river_wolf_pack` is MEASURED-only in sim_combat_batch.gd (RIVERFARM_CELLS, no win-rate contract to hold) -- re-measured, not re-gated; before/after logged there.

River_wolf_pack's second flanker -- see river_wolf_a's _comment for the canon cite + the issue #83 `skirmisher` adoption. Identical stat template (a matched pack pair), given its own id per the distinct-id convention documented on rift_vermin_a.

River_wolf_pack's third member, the pack's alpha -- see river_wolf_a's _comment for the canon cite. Slightly higher stats across the board plus `power_strike` (the pack leader's harder bite) so a 3-wolf night ambush has real teeth without every wolf carrying the same multiplier hit. Stays plain `melee` (issue #83): the alpha holds the line while its two flankers (river_wolf_a/b) skirmish around it.

Invrisil 8c Task C2 (issues #12/#13) -- `alley_footpads_a`/`alley_footpads_b`'s roster (lane alpha wires the two sneakable trigger_radius entities into mercantile_alleys; this lane owns only the combat data they resolve to). ORIGINAL, canon-plausible generic street crime -- the wiki (wiki.wanderinginn.com/Invrisil) attests Invrisil as the huge, wealthy 'City of Adventurers'; no single named petty-mugger gang is on-page distinct from the Brothers themselves, so a plain opportunistic footpad duo is a direct, non-colliding extrapolation (same convention as sewer_vermin/crate_scavengers' generic-diegetic stand-ins). DESIGN CONTRACT (spec sec.5 + the controller's design notes): footpads are SNEAK TARGETS, tuned LOW-lethality by design -- a player who fails the K2 [Stealth] check and gets ambushed must not be walled by a fight, so this pair sits BELOW goblin_raider (str10/con9/die4) on every axis, closer to sewer_vermin's fragile trash-tier. `footpad_lookout` is the leaner, dex-leaning half of the pair (a purse-snatcher, not a brawler). No skills -- a plain shove/grab, not a real weapon technique. Harness: sim_combat_batch.gd INVRISIL_CELLS, gated favoring the floor (0.75-0.98, above the generic 0.55 floor) at warrior2 SOLO (no ally structurally present when sneaking the alleys alone) -- the low-lethality intent as an explicit contract, not a vibe.

Alley_footpads' second member -- see footpad_lookout's own _comment for the canon-plausibility cite + the LOW-lethality design contract. `footpad_bruiser` is the pair's slightly sturdier half (a cudgel-swinger, still deliberately weaker than goblin_raider on every axis) -- an asymmetric-pair shape (lean+sturdy) matching goblin_ambush's raider+shaman and briar_collector_deep's own convention, without escalating overall lethality. Both `alley_footpads_a` and `alley_footpads_b` field this SAME two-combatant pair (lane alpha's two encounter placements, not two different rosters) -- distinct ids per member per the #38 convention, reused verbatim across both encounter entities.

Invrisil 8c Task C2 (issues #12/#13) -- `hired_blades`, the merchant-prince's warehouse roster (lane alpha/C3 wires the encounter entity + the Wilovan come-along beat separately; this lane owns the combat data + arena). The game's FIRST all-human combatant family, per spec sec.2: 'his hired blades = the first all-human combatant family (art: doublets + clubs/knives -- NOT Watch-alike; distinct palette)'. The merchant-prince himself is ORIGINAL+flag (docs/design/character-profiles-staging.md 'Invrisil (8c)'); his hired muscle inherits that same ORIGINAL+flag status -- a respectable merchant paying for thuggery is generic and canon-plausible, not an invented named entity. `hired_blade_leader` is the pair's heavy -- a club-swinging foreman who leads with `power_strike` (the EXISTING skill goblin_chieftain/river_wolf_c already use for a 'pack leader hits harder' read; no new effect type), higher con than the two knife-thugs. Sprite `hired_blade` (owned PixelLab rig, burgundy/brass merchant-livery doublet -- see data/sprites.json's own _comment + assets/LICENSES/pixellab-ai-generated-verdict.md for the full NOT-Watch-alike palette-quarantine rationale) is shared by all 3 roster members, same convention as briar_collector/river_wolf/ruin_ward. Harness: sim_combat_batch.gd INVRISIL_CELLS, GATED 0.6-0.8 with the `wilovan` ally (the deep_descent/ruin_guardian boss-cell precedent for a gated-ally band); the solo cell (declined the come-along beat) is measured-only, the hard-mode frontier, same convention as awakened_boss_w2_solo/ruin_guardian_w8_solo. ISSUE #66 (region tiers): the gating build moved from `warrior5_mage5` to the T3 reference build `t3_spellsword9` (`hired_blades_t3_spellsword9_wilovan`, same 0.6-0.8 band) -- `warrior5_mage5`'s own cell (`hired_blades_w10_wilovan`) is now the measured pre-tier baseline. con raised on all three roster members (leader 18->32, knife_a/knife_b 12->23 each) to hold the 0.6-0.8 band against t3_spellsword9's much higher str; see docs/design/region-tiers.md.
